subject: Sentinel Health — on-prem path pinpoint & NAT/SG triage
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@sentinelhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent file upload failures after private cutover

Hi Jonas —

We cut traffic over to Redwood Private (VPC peering + on-prem gateway) this morning and are seeing intermittent failures from our on-prem backup client to S3 (uploads stall / TCP resets). Failures started ~08:45 PDT. We captured a short pcap and see repeated TCP retransmits then a bunch of ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages.

Symptoms:
- Large multipart uploads (chunks ~64MB) fail ~60% of the time; small files <1MB always succeed
- Failures are seen from two datacenter subnets (10.10.4.0/24 and 10.10.6.0/24)
- When uploads fail, retry within 30s usually succeeds

We suspect path MTU / MSS interaction but also saw different source ports between successes/failures and some NAT rewrite counts spike. Can you take a look? I attached the pcap and a route-dump from our edge.

Thanks,
Amir
NetOps — Sentinel Health

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, amir.patel@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-18T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent file upload failures after private cutover

Thanks Amir — filing an internal triage. Vanessa/Kim: can you join? Initial read: pcap shows lots of ICMP "Fragmentation needed" + TTLs look normal. Two immediate suspects: 

1) MTU / MSS mismatch on the on-prem edge or the customer firewall (we saw this often with GWL/NAT devices that don’t do MSS clamp)
2) SNAT port exhaustion or ephemeral port translation asymmetry — the differing source ports Amir saw could imply double-NAT or a stateful device rewriting return path to a different egress IP.

What I need from you both:
- Vanessa: can you validate the egress MTU and MSS clamp state on the private gateway for the affected routes? Any recent config pushed during cutover?
- Kim: can you pull SNAT metrics for the dedicated NAT pool for Sentinel's tenant (port usage, collisions) and check conntrack evictions for the time window 08:30–09:30 PDT?

I’ll look at packet capture and the edge route dump and share notes.

—Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, amir.patel@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent file upload failures after private cutover

Quick findings after checking the gateway:
- Gateway egress MTU for the tenant route (10.10.0.0/16 -> peer vtn-42) is 1500. No recent MTU changes in the last 48h.
- MSS-clamp was NOT enabled on the GWNAT (we defaulted to no-clamp for TCP offload testing during the cutover).
- I forced a trace to customer IP 54.194.23.9 (S3 endpoint) with DF set; observed ICMP "frag needed" from upstream firewall at 1492 bytes of payload.

Hypothesis: upstream customer firewall or transit path drops fragmented packets when DF is set. With MSS clamp off, client attempts large segments leading to fragmentation failures.

Action I took: enabled MSS-clamp 1400 on gateway for the Sentinel route as a temporary mitigation. Will monitor.

Attachments: edge-route-dump-aug18.txt (route table and policy).

Vanessa
Senior Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, amir.patel@sentinelhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-18T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent file upload failures after private cutover

I pulled SNAT and conntrack metrics for the window Amir reported (08:30–09:30 PDT):
- NAT pool: 10.200.0.0/28 (ports 1024–65535). Peak ephemeral port usage = 87% at 08:42; transient (2–3s) spikes to 95% correlated with high-frequency upload retries.
- Conntrack evictions: ~3200 entries evicted across the NAT cluster during the hour (eviction policy: LRU). Most evictions tagged to tenant-id=sentinel-001.
- No obvious asymmetric return IP observed in NAT logs; return IPs remained consistent for the session tuples I traced.

Interpretation: port pressure getting close to limits during heavy parallel uploads — combined with fragmentation, this leads to retry storms and short-lived port exhaustion. MSS clamp fix should reduce fragmentation, but we should also increase NAT ephemeral pool reservation for sentinel-001 to avoid evictions during high concurrency.

Suggested next steps:
1) Keep MSS-clamp 1400 in place for now (Vanessa).
2) Temporarily reserve an additional NAT pool / increase port range for sentinel-001 (Marissa, can you coordinate billing/tenant config?)
3) Ask Sentinel to stagger parallel upload concurrency (short term).

Kim
Senior SRE — Edge Services
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: amir.patel@sentinelhealth.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent file upload failures after private cutover

Amir — thanks for the patience and for the pcap. Summary of what we did and next steps:

Summary / Root causes identified:
- Primary: Path MTU / fragmentation interaction. Upstream firewall returned ICMP "fragmentation needed" which caused large TCP segments to fail when DF was set. MSS-clamp off at cutover allowed oversized segments.
- Secondary: Ephemeral port pressure on our NAT pool produced transient conntrack evictions under retry storms, amplifying the failure rate for parallel uploads.

What we changed on our side (done):
- Enabled MSS-clamp 1400 on the tenant route at the gateway (Vanessa) — monitoring shows upload success rate jumped to ~95% for retries.
- Temporarily expanded NAT ephemeral allocation for sentinel-001 by adding 2 /28 pools (Kim) — effective immediately for next 48h.
- Increased conntrack table headroom on the NAT cluster to reduce evictions during spikes.

What we suggest you do (Sentinel):
- Stagger upload concurrency to 6–8 parallel streams for the next 24 hours, then we can relax once metrics stabilize.
- If you control the on-prem firewall, validate that ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages are allowed back to the source (or enable MSS clamp there too).

Attachments: packet-capture-2027-08-18.pcap (excerpt), edge-route-dump-aug18.txt

I’ll keep this ticket open for two business days and will follow up with a short post-mortem. If anything regresses ping me directly.

—Marissa
Support Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
